answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with ferrous enclave attestation: each identity must anchor to one hardware enclave that signs a fresh remote-attestation quote, like a ship proving it is moored at a real wharf, not a painted backdrop. A farm needs a separate ferrous chip for every fake, and chips cannot be cloned or run in parallel, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand devices. One honest agent uses the enclave it already has, and its attestation streaks across the ledger like a comet: cheap to verify, costly to counterfeit in bulk.
